name: WOO X
rootCause: A targeted social engineering attack attributed to North Korea's Lazarus Group (UNC4899) compromised a WOO X developer's device. The attacker posed as an open-source collaborator and convinced a developer to download a malicious debugging tool; after antivirus scans returned clean, the developer ran the file on a company MacBook, which deployed a hidden backdoor that evaded detection by masquerading as a common backend process. Over approximately two hours the attacker used this foothold to authorize unauthorized withdrawals from nine user accounts across BTC, ETH, BNB, Arbitrum, and Tron networks, draining $14 million before the breach was detected and contained. All affected users were fully reimbursed by WOO X from its treasury. Attack Tx: 0x9099c84152dbdc72d84affb257b51b5bc67e349fb4beb67c41e1a37491f3ed24 Analysis: July 24th - Security incident post-mortem (WOO X)

descriptions.text: $14 million lost on WOO X when a phishing attack compromised a team member's device, giving hackers access to wallets across multiple blockchains. Third strike for WOO ecosystem after $25 million Kronos and $8.5 million WooFi breaches - turning their best-in-class security into a joke.

Crypto trading platform WOO X suffered an attack resulting in a loss of approximately $14 million. According to the official disclosure, the incident stemmed from a targeted phishing attack that compromised a team member’s device, allowing the attacker to gain access to the development environment.

On July 24, 2025, WOO X suffered a breach after an attacker used a phishing campaign to compromise a developer’s device, ultimately gaining persistent access to the cloud production environment. The attacker escalated privileges and used extracted database credentials to coordinate unauthorized withdrawals from nine user accounts, totaling $14 million across multiple chains. The incident was contained within hours, with all affected users compensated and withdrawals temporarily suspended for a security review. Attackers who compromised devices belonging to a WOO X employee stole $14 million from users of the Taiwanese WOO X cryptocurrency exchange. The phishing attack on the employee gave the hackers access to a development environment, according to statements from WOO X, and the hackers were then able to make withdrawals from customer accounts. WOO X temporarily froze withdrawals, before reopening accounts after a security review. They offered a 10% " bounty " to the thief.
